title: Ali G’s return sparks wave of criticism in Britain - BGNES
content: The revival of the comedy character Ali G, played by actor Sacha Baron Cohen, has already sparked controversy in Britain, The Independent reported. NewsCord, a British news comparison website, has launched a campaign calling on cinemas around the world to refuse to screen the upcoming mockumentary Ali G: Who Are Ya?, while Picturehouse Cinemas, which operates 25 cinemas across the UK, responded to the campaign by saying it has no plans to screen the film. The film, distributed by Amazon MGM, is in a mock-documentary style similar to Borat and features Baron Cohen interacting with unsuspecting members of the public in character as Ali G, a character created by the actor in 1998 and previously featured in the 2002 feature film Ali G Indahouse. NewsCord’s campaign claims that the character perpetuates harmful stereotypes, citing criticism from Black British comedians dating back to 2000, when he was described as an “alibi for racism”, as well as comments by writer Jeanette Winterson and Kazakh and Arab organisations. According to the website, more than 37,000 emails have been sent in support of the campaign. In a statement to Metro, Picturehouse confirmed that it “currently has no plans to screen this film on release”. When the character first appeared in 1998, comedians including Curtis Walker and Felix Dexter criticised him. Dexter described the humour as a way for the liberal middle classes to laugh at Black street culture while maintaining a sense of political correctness. Baron Cohen himself said in 2016 on the WTF with Marc Maron podcast that the character had been conceived partly as a subtle attempt to undermine the established social order. According to the synopsis of the new film, the story takes place 20 years after the original series, when Ali G discovers that his long-term girlfriend Julie is pregnant and travels to America to reclaim his former fame, facing opponents who threaten his existence and the future of his child. The film is scheduled for release on 23 October. | BGNES The content of this web site, such as texts, video, graphics and images, may only be used with the written consent of BGNES. title: No 2027 Federal Pay Raise: Freeze Base and Locality Pay at 2026 Rates - MyFederalRetirement
content:
Financial Planning Resources for Federal & Postal Employees President Trump has formally frozen federal civilian pay for 2027, transmitting his alternative pay plan letter to Congress on August 26. The letter proposes holding both base pay and locality pay at 2026 rates for most federal employees, while authorizing a 3.8% increase for law enforcement personnel and raises of 5% to 7% for military members, depending on rank. Congress can still override the freeze, but has not done so in similar years past, and the alternative pay plan typically becomes final when OPM issues the official 2027 pay tables in December. If it stands, 2027 would be the smallest civilian pay adjustment since the freeze years of the early 2010s. Enter your email  on this form [CLICK HERE] (opens in new tab)and we’ll send you an email alert as soon as the 2027 pay raise (or freeze) is finalized — plus what it means for your specific grade and step. The letter cites(opens in new tab) the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act (FEPCA), which requires the president to submit an alternative pay plan each year by August 31 or allow a statutory formula to take effect automatically. According to the letter, that formula would have triggered locality pay increases averaging 20.6% at a cost of $26 billion in the first year, on top of a 3.1% across-the-board base pay increase. The administration says freezing pay avoids that cost. OPM has not yet said which categories of law enforcement personnel will qualify for the 3.8% increase; that determination is expected to follow the same process used for the 2026 raise. These two figures get confused every year, and this year is no different. The federal pay raise applies only to current employees and is set through the political process described above. The COLA applies to retirees and is calculated automatically from the Consumer Price Index, with no input from the president or Congress. The 2027 COLA will be announced in October once third-quarter CPI-W data are final, with early estimates pointing to a range of roughly 3.5% to 3.7%. If you’re within a few years of retiring, a frozen salary year does more than just hold your paycheck flat. It also affects your High-3 salary average, since that figure is built from your highest 36 consecutive months of basic pay. A year with no raise pulls that average down slightly compared to a year where pay kept rising, and the effect compounds if your final year of service happens to fall during the freeze. Here’s a simplified illustration. Assume a FERS employee earning $114,000, with 2% annual raises in a normal year, compared to the same employee whose final year is frozen at 0%. In this example, the frozen year lowers the High-3 average by about $775. Multiplied by your years of service and pension multiplier, that’s a modest but real reduction to your annuity for the rest of your retirement. It’s not large enough to change most people’s retirement plans on its own, but it’s worth factoring in if you’re deciding between retiring at year-end versus waiting for a possible raise, or if you’re already running the numbers on when to file. A frozen across-the-board and locality rate doesn’t mean your paycheck is completely stuck. Within-grade step increases still apply on their normal schedule if you’re not already at the top step, and any promotion or locality area change still raises your pay. Those factors can offset some or all of the freeze’s effect on your High-3, depending on where you are in your career. Congress has until the alternative pay plan takes effect to pass legislation setting a different number, most likely through the FAIR Act, which would provide a 4.1% raise. That bill has been introduced every year since 2014 and has never passed. Barring a change, OPM will issue the final 2027 pay tables in December, and the freeze outlined in this letter will take effect on the first pay period of January 2027. Gold is projected to extend its recent gains in the second half of 2026, even as growing use of some derivatives tied to the metal could be making gold prices more volatile, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Goldman Sachs Research forecasts the precious metal will rise to $4,900 per troy ounce by the end of the year. Gold rallied 15% from its mid-July low to around $4,600 per troy ounce as of August 25. The metal is expected to rise as central banks continue diversifying their reserves and markets scale back expectations for US rate hikes in 2026. Demand for gold from central banks is a key structural factor underpinning the metal’s rally, according to Lina Thomas, senior commodities analyst in Goldman Sachs Research, and Daan Struyven, co-head of Global Commodities Research. “We continue to see elevated central bank gold accumulation as a multi-year trend, as central banks diversify their reserves to hedge geopolitical and financial risks, consistent with recent survey evidence,” Thomas and Struyven write. Central banks have been diversifying their holdings using gold, which is considered less likely to be frozen than reserves held in foreign currencies. They have been buying gold at an increased rate since 2022, when G7 countries responded to the invasion of Ukraine by freezing Russian central bank assets in Europe. Goldman Sachs Research expects central banks to buy an average of 50 tonnes of gold per month in 2026, up from an average of 17 tonnes per month before 2022. Central bank purchases accelerated to 100 tonnes per month in June 2026 (on a three-month seasonally adjusted basis) from 66 tonnes the previous month, according to Goldman Sachs Research’s nowcast of central bank activity. China’s central bank was the largest identifiable buyer in the market in June. Interest rate expectations are another important factor supporting recent gold price increases. Demand from some investors is starting to recover from a slow first half of the year as markets scale back expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in 2026. Historically, gold tends to struggle when interest rates rise, as higher rates reduce the appeal of gold relative to yielding assets like bonds. “We expect the Fed-related headwind to abate further, as our economists expect a lower inflation trend to keep the Fed on hold this year,” Thomas and Struyven write. The researchers also highlight a range of medium-term factors that could cause the gold price to exceed Goldman Sachs Research’s forecast for 2026. “Gold’s share in private portfolios remains low, and recent geopolitical developments—including Iran and broader tensions—may accelerate diversification beyond central banks to private investors, including by weighing on perceptions of Western fiscal sustainability.” Demand for gold call options is rising as investors turn to the instruments to hedge their portfolios against large-scale changes in government policies. This has the potential to amplify price swings in both directions, Thomas and Struyven explain. As gold rises, it is approaching key strike levels for some call options, forcing options dealers that sold these calls to buy gold in order to hedge their short exposure to the metal, accelerating the rally. On the other hand, declines in the gold price could prompt dealers to reverse those hedges by selling their gold holdings, driving prices even lower. Goldman Sachs Research’s forecast for gold to reach $4,900 per troy ounce by the end of 2026 does not incorporate elevated demand for hedges through gold derivatives. This could increase the likelihood that the gold price exceeds the forecast, but it also suggests “greater two-sided volatility” to the gold rally, Thomas and Struyven write. title: BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy Namibia Recap — Video - Motorcycle.com
content: Ahead of the BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy 2026 taking place in Romania, we thought we’d take a look back at our time alongside Team USA during the 2024 event in Namibia. To recap, 22 teams – 16 men’s, and 6 women’s – arrived in Windhoek to compete against each other and the unforgiving terrain of the African continent. Though some of the landscape was similar to the American Southwest, coming around a corner to a herd of giraffes, wildebeest or oryx quickly reminded one that they were not in Kansas (North Carolina, Texas, or Florida) anymore. Representing Team USA was Kirk Graydon from South Carolina, Billy De Wet from Texas via South Africa, and Scott Acheson from Florida. Regrettably, the American women's qualifying team was unable to advance past the semi-final rounds during this year's competition. For this event, the teams would be competing on the then-new BMW R 1300 GS, BMW’s flagship adventure machine which received a massive update for the model year. With the event in its ninth edition, we’d span 1,300 km, competing and building lasting friendships with riders from all over the world as the team took on the daily challenges and battled the Namibian outback. It truly was a once in a lifetime experience that the competitors will hold with them forever. For 2026, GS Trophy contenders will compete in the wilds of Romania where dense forests, intense elevation changes, and river crossings will surely test each rider’s mettle as they take on the challenge. For equipment, BMW’s retro-scrambler, the R 12 G/S gets the full Trophy treatment, adding a touch of nostalgia to the event while offering real adventure capability. Hopefully this video recap can serve as an appetizer for the 2026 GS Trophy. To the competitors, good luck and soak up every moment of the journey. title: BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition Marks a Brazilian Milestone - stupidDOPE
content: A factory anniversary can easily become an exercise in commemorative badges and ceremonial paint. BMW Motorrad has taken a more considered route in Brazil, using the R 1300 GS Adventure to connect a decade of motorcycle production in Manaus with a significant manufacturing milestone. The resulting BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition is limited to just ten motorcycles, one representing each year of operation at the Brazilian facility. The choice of model carries particular weight. The R 1300 GS Adventure was also the 150,000th motorcycle produced at the Manaus plant, making the flagship adventure bike more than a convenient platform for a special edition. It represents both the scale BMW’s Brazilian operation has reached and the increasingly international manufacturing footprint behind one of motorcycling‘s most recognizable nameplates. Each anniversary motorcycle receives a deep olive-drab finish accented by yellow pinstriping and exclusive graphics across the fuel tank, side panels, and top case. An Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust adds another distinguishing element, while BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant introduces a more consequential technological feature. The 1,300cc boxer engine remains mechanically unchanged, producing a claimed 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque. For a motorcycle already positioned near the top of BMW’s adventure range, the significance of this edition comes less from additional performance than from context. It connects an important motorcycle, a manufacturing landmark, and BMW Motorrad’s decade-long presence in Manaus through a production run small enough to function almost as a set of rolling historical markers. The tenth anniversary matters because BMW’s Manaus operation represents more than an assembly point serving a regional market. Reaching 150,000 motorcycles demonstrates sustained production at a meaningful scale, and selecting the R 1300 GS Adventure as the milestone machine connects that industrial achievement to one of BMW Motorrad’s most globally recognizable products. Brazil presents compelling reasons for localized motorcycle production. It is one of the world’s substantial motorcycle markets, with two-wheel transportation serving roles ranging from daily mobility to recreation and premium touring. Manaus, meanwhile, has long been an important manufacturing center through the Manaus Free Trade Zone, where industrial policy has encouraged domestic production across numerous sectors. BMW Motorrad’s presence there places the German company’s engineering culture within a distinctly Brazilian manufacturing context. That matters because modern premium vehicles are increasingly international products even when their brand identities remain closely tied to their countries of origin. The R 1300 GS Adventure captures that reality particularly well. Its engineering lineage is unmistakably BMW, from the boxer engine architecture to the chassis philosophy and electronics surrounding it. Yet this particular group of motorcycles also represents ten years of Brazilian production capability. The anniversary edition consequently commemorates people and infrastructure as much as machinery. Limited-edition motorcycles are common, but the logic behind their production numbers can sometimes feel arbitrary. A run of 500 or 1,000 examples creates scarcity, yet the number itself rarely contributes much to the story. BMW’s decision to produce ten examples is considerably more direct. One motorcycle represents each year of operation at the Manaus factory. That makes the limited quantity part of the commemorative concept rather than simply a mechanism for creating exclusivity. Numbering each example strengthens that connection. These motorcycles are not merely R 1300 GS Adventures equipped with an unusual paint package. Each occupies a specific place within a deliberately tiny production series linked to the facility’s history. That distinction will likely matter most over time. Special-edition motorcycles frequently become more interesting as the events they commemorate move further into the past. Production anniversaries, engineering transitions, final editions, competition victories, and factory milestones provide collectors with historical reference points that ordinary colorways cannot. The Manaus edition has two such anchors: the factory’s tenth anniversary and its 150,000th motorcycle. The deep olive-drab finish is particularly appropriate for the R 1300 GS Adventure. Adventure motorcycles already borrow some of their visual identity from expedition equipment. Large fuel tanks, exposed structural components, protective hardware, luggage systems, tall suspension, substantial windscreens, and upright ergonomics communicate purpose before the engine is even started. Olive drab pushes those associations toward military and field equipment without turning the motorcycle into a literal historical reference. Yellow pinstriping provides the necessary counterpoint. Against the muted bodywork, the brighter linework emphasizes the shape of the motorcycle while preventing the finish from becoming visually flat. Exclusive graphics across the tank and side panels establish the anniversary identity, while extending the treatment to the top case makes the luggage feel integrated into the design rather than attached afterward. Cases and other touring equipment occupy significant visual space, and mismatched accessories can disrupt an otherwise carefully developed design. Treating the top case as part of the commemorative package reinforces the sense that the edition was conceived as a complete motorcycle. The palette also avoids one of the more common problems with anniversary products: excessive decoration. BMW does not need gold surfaces, oversized dates, or elaborate graphics to communicate significance. The restrained finish suits a machine whose reputation was built around capability. The GS name carries unusual weight within BMW Motorrad. BMW’s adventure-bike lineage stretches back decades, and the GS family helped establish the template for large-displacement adventure motorcycles long before the segment became one of the industry’s most competitive categories. The formula combined long-distance road ability with off-pavement capability, upright ergonomics, luggage capacity, and the company’s horizontally opposed boxer engine. Modern GS models have become considerably more sophisticated, but that central proposition remains recognizable. The R 1300 GS generation represents a substantial evolution of the formula. Its 1,300cc boxer engine delivers 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque, output substantial enough to handle highway touring, luggage, passengers, steep grades, and off-road situations where careful throttle control becomes more important than outright power. The Adventure version expands the platform’s long-distance intent. That makes it particularly fitting as a factory milestone. A 150,000th motorcycle could have been almost any model on the production schedule. Having the number land on the R 1300 GS Adventure gives BMW a machine capable of representing the breadth of its modern engineering approach. It is technologically sophisticated, historically recognizable, and built for the kind of large-scale travel with which the GS identity has become synonymous. BMW has resisted the temptation to increase engine output simply to distinguish the anniversary edition. The familiar 1,300cc boxer remains rated at 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque. Special editions do not automatically become better when manufacturers increase power. On a large adventure motorcycle, additional output can have limited practical value compared with improvements in control, ergonomics, suspension behavior, heat management, reliability, or rider assistance. The existing engine already provides considerable performance. More importantly, the horizontally opposed twin remains fundamental to the GS experience. Its low-mounted cylinders contribute to the motorcycle’s recognizable silhouette while helping position substantial engine mass lower in the chassis. Decades of development have transformed the boxer from a historical curiosity into a highly sophisticated modern powerplant. Leaving it mechanically intact keeps the anniversary edition connected to the standard motorcycle rather than creating an unnecessarily altered derivative. BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant is arguably the anniversary edition’s most consequential equipment feature. The system replaces conventional manual clutch operation with electronic actuators capable of managing clutch and gear changes. Riders can retain control over shifting when desired or allow the motorcycle to handle gear selection automatically. That creates an interesting evolution for a category traditionally associated with mechanical rider involvement. Manual transmissions have long been treated as an essential part of motorcycling because clutch and gear selection contribute directly to the physical relationship between rider and machine. Automation inevitably raises questions about whether convenience removes part of that connection. BMW’s approach is more nuanced because it preserves choice. A rider can still select gears manually without managing a traditional clutch lever, while automatic operation becomes available when circumstances make it preferable. Heavy traffic, extended touring, fatigue, or repetitive low-speed riding can all make reduced clutch work attractive. Adventure motorcycles present a particularly interesting use case because their operating environments vary so dramatically. A rider might spend hours covering highway distance, navigate stop-and-go city traffic, climb winding mountain roads, and eventually encounter loose surfaces or technical terrain. A transmission system capable of changing behavior across those situations has legitimate value. Rather than simply making the R 1300 GS Adventure easier, the technology attempts to make it more adaptable. The Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust provides a more traditional premium upgrade. Akrapovič has become deeply established within high-end motorcycle culture, with its exhaust systems appearing across everything from road-going sport bikes to racing machinery and adventure motorcycles. The brand’s reputation comes from a combination of materials expertise, weight reduction, acoustic tuning, performance development, and manufacturing quality. On the anniversary R 1300 GS Adventure, the dual slip-on configuration provides a visible distinction from standard equipment while complementing the motorcycle’s premium positioning. The exhaust also introduces another sensory element. Motorcycles are experienced through sound and vibration as much as visual design. An exhaust system can change the character of an otherwise familiar powertrain without requiring fundamental engine modifications. That makes the Akrapovič system a logical addition to a commemorative model whose engine output remains standard. It adds personality without disrupting the proven mechanical foundation. The R 1300 GS Adventure also illustrates how dramatically the adventure category has evolved. Early adventure motorcycles were comparatively simple machines whose appeal came partly from mechanical straightforwardness. Modern flagship ADV bikes increasingly resemble technological showcases, incorporating sophisticated electronics, electronically managed suspension, advanced braking systems, selectable riding modes, navigation integration, radar-based assistance on some models, and increasingly automated drivetrain functions. This evolution reflects what riders ask these motorcycles to do. A modern adventure bike may serve as a commuter, interstate touring machine, weekend canyon motorcycle, two-up traveler, gravel-road explorer, and long-distance expedition platform. That breadth requires compromises, but it also rewards adaptable technology. BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant belongs within that trajectory. Purists may prefer complete manual control, and simpler motorcycles retain advantages in cost, weight, familiarity, and field serviceability. Yet the growth of electronic assistance does not necessarily contradict adventure riding. Technology can reduce workload during mundane sections and preserve rider attention for situations that demand it. The anniversary edition therefore represents more than ten years of factory production. It also captures where the GS concept has arrived technologically. Perhaps the most interesting aspect of the R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition is the geography behind it. BMW remains inseparable from German engineering culture, yet the Manaus edition demonstrates how international the production of premium vehicles has become. Manufacturing expertise does not remain confined to the location where a brand was founded. A Brazilian-built anniversary GS makes that reality visible. For the Manaus workforce, the 150,000-unit milestone represents accumulated manufacturing experience. For BMW, it demonstrates the ability to maintain a premium product identity across an international production network. For collectors, the ten motorcycles connect those industrial circumstances to a physical object. That gives the edition a kind of authenticity that cannot be created solely through cosmetic customization. The olive-drab paint, yellow pinstriping, numbered production, exclusive graphics, Akrapovič exhaust, and Automated Shift Assistant all contribute to desirability. Yet the motorcycle’s real distinction comes from what it represents. The best commemorative vehicles make their special status easy to explain decades later. The BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition already has that advantage. It celebrates ten years of production at BMW’s Manaus factory, arrives as a ten-unit numbered series, and uses the same model that became the facility’s 150,000th motorcycle. Its specifications reinforce the story without overwhelming it. The deep olive-drab finish and yellow pinstriping establish a distinct visual identity. The Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust gives the motorcycle an appropriate premium hardware upgrade. Automated Shift Assistant demonstrates where BMW’s touring technology is heading. Meanwhile, the unchanged 145-horsepower boxer preserves the mechanical character of the underlying R 1300 GS Adventure. That balance is important. Anniversary models often become collections of options assembled around a commemorative badge. This edition has a clearer reason to exist because the motorcycle itself is directly tied to the event being celebrated. Only ten examples ensure that relatively few riders will ever own one, but scarcity is not the most interesting part of the project. The Manaus edition captures a specific moment in BMW Motorrad’s manufacturing history while demonstrating how far the GS has evolved from its comparatively elemental adventure-bike origins. FPS players need hair-trigger inputs for fast movement and aiming. Racers, meanwhile, are looking for finer control for steering and acceleration. As your skills improve, how you use your keyboard will change, too. Logitech G gaming keyboards are meant to be flexible. You don’t need to compromise on a keyboard that isn’t the right fit, because keyboards like the G 512 X and G 316 X are fully customizable to help you play your own way. Nobody can know what works for them straight away. It’s all about the fine-tuning. The Logitech G512 X has two actuation points to set how far you need to press a key before it registers, allowing one key to trigger one action with a light press and another on a full press. The included SAPP rings give you a tactile bump at that second point so you can feel exactly when it activates. The result is a board that gives you huge control over how quickly it responds. What about the layout? Logitech's G512 X 75 strips away the numpad and function keys. The G512 X 98 gives them all back. It’s the same core keyboard either way, but you get to choose how many keys you need and how much space it takes up on your desk. Customization doesn’t have to mean deep-diving into a long settings menu. The Logitech G316 X takes a simpler approach, putting everyday controls directly onto the keyboard. Its onboard dial and dot-matrix LED display let you quickly switch settings such as volume, media, and brightness, as well as your keyboard’s polling rate. Its mechanical switches are hot-swappable too, with customizable PBT keycaps that let you change the board's look and feel. Competitive players don’t settle. They’re always looking for tiny improvements to their game. Logitech G keyboards give you the space to step out of your comfort zone and try out new techniques. This is where the Logitech G512 X comes into its own. The G512 X has 39 dual-swap keys that let you switch between TMR (tunnel magnetoresistance) analog and traditional mechanical switches. TMR switches recognize how far you press a key, rather than just whether or not you’ve pressed it. A lighter press might let you ease around a corner while you’re racing, or push further when you want maximum acceleration. Analog input for your WASD keys adds precision to your gameplay, giving games a range of inputs. Here’s an example: You’re playing F1 2026, and you want to go — and go fast. With TMR analog switches, your acceleration isn’t just on or off; it’s zero to 100%, depending on how hard you press that W key. You can then use mechanical switches for abilities where a simple keypress works best. You’ve got the freedom to build your keyboard around the games you play, with functionality that doesn’t get in the way. You don't need to be a pro to get in on the action. The G316 X’s minimalist design and straightforward configuration give you a serious-looking setup without hours of unnecessarily complicated settings to wade through. Its gasket-mounted construction and sound-dampening layers shape how the keyboard feels and sounds, while configurable RGB lighting lets you customize the look. The same QWERTY keys might look identical, but individual game profiles mean they don't have to act the same way. Rather than rebuilding your controls each time, you can save your key preferences, shortcuts, and macros for each game, and the G Hub app loads your presets automatically when you launch. That leaves you with a choice: Which Logitech G keyboard is the one? The G316 X is beginner-friendly, with hot-swappable mechanical switches and onboard controls that are easy to master. The G512 X models are for players who want to get into the weeds, with adjustable actuation and much more control over how individual keys respond. Logitech designed these keyboards to let you play your way. Your keyboard isn’t set in stone. It’s something you can shape around your games, preferences, and playstyle. title: SOOSAN INT's eSafe AI V3 Wins Top GS Certification - thelec.net
content: SOOSAN INT's generative artificial intelligence (AI) gateway solution, eSafe AI V3, has received Grade 1 certification under the Good Software (GS) quality certification program. SOOSAN INT said the Grade 1 certification officially validates the software quality and product maturity of eSafe AI V3. The cybersecurity company plans to use the certification to strengthen its push into the enterprise market, including public institutions and the financial, manufacturing and IT sectors, where the use of generative AI is expanding. GS certification is a nationally recognized quality certification that comprehensively evaluates software in areas including functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability, portability, performance, interoperability, connectivity and compliance. Certified products are eligible for support in public-sector procurement, including contracts with the Public Procurement Service and registration on the Korea ON-line E-Procurement System, and can receive preferential consideration in public information technology projects. eSafe AI V3 is an integrated generative AI platform tailored to AI environments and a generative AI prompt security solution incorporating data loss prevention (DLP) capabilities. According to SOOSAN INT, the product allows multiple large language model (LLM) platforms to be used and managed through a single interface, while detecting and blocking in real time potential leaks involving prompt inputs, keywords, attachments and personal information. The platform also allows organizations to centrally manage multiple generative AI services, providing visibility into AI use and enabling consistent application of security policies. Organizations can establish security governance policies by setting differentiated access permissions for individual users and departments. The platform also provides real-time analysis of usage, token consumption and costs associated with AI services, and allows administrators to set usage limits.

title: GS Retail launches marine conservation and recycling campaigns - 헤럴드경제
content: Photo exhibition and e-waste collection drive held ahead of Resource Circulation Day GS Retail is hosting a photo exhibition for its marine environmental protection campaign, the "Bada Sum Project," at GS Tower in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, through Sept. 5. Running since last year, the Bada Sum Project is a marine conservation initiative carried out in partnership with the Ocean and East Asia Sea Community (OSEAN) and marine exploration group Team Booster. The campaign aims to improve marine habitats and preserve biodiversity through ocean debris collection and underwater ecosystem cleanup and monitoring. The exhibition, timed ahead of Resource Circulation Day on Sept. 6, features more than 40 photographs of marine life and underwater ecosystems taken by underwater photographers from Team Booster. Last year, the project focused on protecting sea turtle migration routes off Jeju and in the East Sea. This year, the effort continued in Yangyang with conservation activities for eelgrass, a protected marine species. GS Retail is also running a resource circulation drive to recycle discarded electronics. As part of its "Our Neighborhood Resource Circulation Campaign," the company will hold an e-waste collection event at GS Tower on Wednesday. GS Retail employees, GS Group affiliates and GS25 franchise owners are invited to participate. Collected items will be processed and recycled through E-Cycle Governance. On the same day, GS Retail will offer employees an environmental education session that includes a hands-on microplastics sorting activity. GS Retail plans to continue expanding its resource circulation efforts, drawing on a network of more than 18,000 stores nationwide under GS25 and GS The Fresh. "We will continue to carry out ESG activities that employees and franchise owners can take part in together," said Park Gyeong-rang, head of GS Retail's ESG division.

title: Karol G's 'Bby Wow' Hits No. 1 — And the Song It Dethroned Was Her Own - Latin Times
content: Karol G just did something almost nobody pulls off in Latin music: she took her own song down from the top spot. "Bby Wow," her team-up with Judeline and Rusowsky, vaulted from No. 5 to No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs chart for the week of Aug. 29, edging out her own hit "Ahí" with Drake, which slides to No. 4. It's the Medellín singer's 11th trip to No. 1 on that chart, and it's a feat no act has managed against themselves in almost two years. For the two Spanish artists riding shotgun on the track, reaching No. 1 is a first-time milestone in more ways than one — "Bby Wow" also became their debut chart-topper on Billboard's Hot Latin Rhythm Songs list, where it likewise jumped from fifth to first, and Billboard flagged it as the top-ranked pairing involving a Latin act currently sitting on that particular list. Judeline, whose given name is Lara Fernández Castrelo, told Billboard she's still catching up to how quickly it all happened, saying it's "hard to believe a song we recorded last month is already topping the charts." Her fingerprints are on more than just that one song — she has writing credits on four tracks from the album altogether, a list that also includes "Matadora" (it entered at No. 4) and "Te Llevas To" (No. 6), both of which arrived on Hot Latin Songs the week before "Bby Wow" took over. The single's climb is one piece of a much bigger takeover. Karol G's sixth studio album, "No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto," out since Aug. 7, marked her fifth trip to the top of Billboard's Top Latin Albums chart and is now holding that position for a second consecutive week. At the peak of its rollout, 13 different songs from the record crowded onto Hot Latin Songs in a single week — a stretch that also produced guest turns from Drake and Bruno Mars. "Bby Wow" pulled in 6.1 million official U.S. on-demand streams in its tracking week, per Luminate figures cited by Billboard, and reached as far as position No. 38 on Billboard's all-genre Hot 100 tally, Karol G's best showing there in two years. "Ahí" wasn't a slouch either: its debut brought in 11.8 million streams worldwide, good for No. 44 on the Hot 100 and a berth at No. 103 on the Global 200, while "Still," the record's collaboration with Bruno Mars, notched the set's strongest Hot 100 opening at No. 41. There's a live-show angle here that matters for two of the audiences this outlet covers most closely. Karol G's "Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour" already got underway — she kicked things off with a pair of packed shows in Chicago back in late July — and the trek is now working its way toward Texas and Florida. It's set to stop at Houston's Reliant Stadium on Sept. 27 before landing at Miami Gardens' Hard Rock Stadium for two nights, Oct. 2 and Oct. 3, according to tour listings on Ticketmaster. For South Florida, the Hard Rock dates carry extra weight: it will be Karol G's first performance in the Miami market since August 2023, when she played the city on her "Mañana Será Bonito" tour, NBC 6 South Florida reported when the tour was first announced. Fans catching either stop this fall are likely to hear "Ahí" and "Bby Wow" fresh off their runs atop the Latin charts, alongside deeper cuts from a record that's currently dominating the genre almost on its own. What the past two chart weeks really show has less to do with any single track and more to do with how much ground Karol G is currently holding. "DTMF" no longer sits at No. 1, but it hasn't fallen out of the upper tier either — it's remained parked at No. 2 through the entire changeover. Karol G, meanwhile, has now spent back-to-back weeks running the very top of the chart with two different songs pulled from the same album. Not many acts have pulled off that particular trick: Bad Bunny is the only other recent example, back when his single "Nuevayol" gave way to his own "DTMF" as 2025 began. Among women, Karol G is the only one to have done it before — her own 2023 single "Qlona," featuring Peso Pluma, is what dethroned "Mi Ex Tenía Razón" that year. For scale, the longest No. 1 run of 2024 on this same chart was Karol G's own "Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido," which lasted 14 weeks — a fraction of "DTMF's" 72-week hold. Whether "Bby Wow" can stay on top anywhere near that long is the question next week's chart data will start to answer. © {{Year}} Latin Times. All rights reserved. title: SEC Probe Puts Wall Street Leverage Risk Back in Focus - MarketBeat
content:
When a high-flying fund crashes, the shockwaves can spill beyond its own balance sheet. Following a sharp mid-summer sell-off in the semiconductor sector, the artificial intelligence-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness sustained a devastating 67% portfolio drawdown. To meet escalating margin calls, the fund liquidated the bulk of its public equities at a steep discount. Now, regulators are asking hard questions about the institutions that bankrolled those trades. The Securities and Exchange Commission recently issued subpoenas to four major Wall Street prime brokers. Regulators want to understand the timing of the fund's trades, its communications with lenders, and how these banks monitored such aggressive leverage. While a regulatory inquiry of this magnitude might sound the alarm for a systemic banking sector crisis, a closer look at the underlying fundamentals tells a different story. The immediate threat does not lie in bank insolvency. The more relevant risk investors need to watch for is the potential for a forced, market-wide deleveraging cycle. To understand how the market is digesting this regulatory probe, it helps to look at the financial health of the prime brokers involved. The fundamental baseline for these institutions is incredibly strong, creating a meaningful buffer against immediate liquidity stress. During the most recent quarter, The Goldman Sachs Group NYSE: GS delivered a substantial earnings beat. Goldman Sachs topped consensus earnings per share estimates by over $6.50, while revenue rose nearly 40% year-over-year. Similarly, JPMorgan Chase & Co. NYSE: JPM beat consensus estimates by approximately 55 cents per share, backed by a revenue jump of around 27%. These are not institutions showing signs of immediate balance-sheet distress; they are generating billions in operating cash flow. Capital return programs also signal management confidence and provide a solid floor for equity valuations. Bank of America NYSE: BAC recently authorized an approximately $40 billion share repurchase program, which could retire up to 11% of its outstanding stock. Retiring shares reduces the overall float, ultimately boosting future earnings per share. Citigroup Inc. NYSE: C is actively executing an approximately $30 billion buyback plan of its own, targeting up to 13.7% of its shares. Market positioning reflects this fundamental stability. Short interest across all four of these banking giants remains at healthy, normalized levels. Institutional short-sellers are not aggressively betting against these equities, suggesting the broader market views the Situational Awareness collapse as an isolated incident rather than a systemic failure in prime brokerage. If the banks are fundamentally sound, the natural question is why the Securities and Exchange Commission is issuing subpoenas. The answer lies in the mechanics of margin lending and counterparty risk management. Prime brokers provide hedge funds with the capital needed to amplify their trades. In the case of Situational Awareness, the fund reportedly used heavy leverage, with some reports describing leverage near four times gross exposure. For every dollar of core capital, the fund borrowed roughly three dollars to maximize its exposure to the booming artificial intelligence (AI) trade. When the underlying semiconductor stocks reversed course, those amplified gains quickly turned into accelerated losses. The Securities and Exchange Commission is currently in a discovery phase, investigating how Wall Street facilitates and manages the risk profile of a single, highly concentrated fund. Regulators are scrutinizing internal risk-monitoring protocols to determine whether Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, and Bank of America took on excessive risk by maintaining such elevated leverage. They are also reportedly examining the efficacy and timing of the subsequent margin calls. When a leveraged fund experiences a severe drawdown, its prime broker issues margin calls requiring the fund to deposit additional cash or sell assets to cover the borrowed funds. If the fund cannot provide cash, it must liquidate holdings. In crowded sectors like semiconductors, forced selling can drive asset prices down further, triggering additional margin calls for other funds holding the same assets. The central issue is whether this extreme leverage points to a broader vulnerability in how prime brokers monitor clients. Regulators want to ensure that if a few heavily leveraged funds face sudden drawdowns, the resulting margin calls do not create localized liquidity vacuums or disrupt the broader financial system. The immediate downside risk to financial equities appears contained by their strong balance sheets, but the downstream risk to the broader market warrants careful attention. If the Securities and Exchange Commission uncovers systemic weaknesses in how Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, or Bank of America monitor client leverage, regulators could mandate stricter capital requirements or tighter oversight on margin lending. Even without a direct regulatory mandate, prime brokers might preemptively tighten their financing terms to avoid further scrutiny and mitigate their own counterparty risk. A credit-tightening cycle in the prime brokerage space creates ripple effects across the financial landscape. Hedge funds heavily reliant on borrowed capital would face higher margin requirements and reduced borrowing capacity. To meet these new constraints, funds would be forced to unwind positions and sell assets, draining liquidity from the market. This potential deleveraging event intersects with notable macroeconomic headwinds. The upcoming September Federal Open Market Committee meeting adds complexity. If interest rates remain elevated for longer than anticipated, the cost of carrying heavy leverage compounds. A scenario in which borrowing costs remain high while prime brokers simultaneously restrict access to margin could accelerate forced-liquidation pressure across the entire hedge fund sector. Wall Street's largest prime brokers possess the capital reserves and fundamental strength to weather this specific regulatory inquiry. The 67% wipeout was strictly due to Situational Awareness, not to the banking institutions that financed the trades. Regulatory spotlights alter institutional behavior. As prime brokers review their internal risk models and prepare to answer subpoenas, the availability of easy, cheap leverage may begin to shrink. When credit terms tighten, highly leveraged market participants are usually the first to feel the squeeze, often leading to sudden bursts of volatility in crowded trades. Investors may want to evaluate their portfolios for exposure to sectors favored by leveraged funds. Monitoring how JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs adjust their margin lending practices in the coming months can provide valuable clues about where broader market liquidity might tighten next. title: New bodega bringing 1920s style to St. Cloud's East End - St. Cloud Times
content: A new 1920s-style convenience store is coming to St. Cloud's East End. Marla Waseka owns the building under MoXie Ladies, LLC and will operate St. G's Bodega with her two daughters. Bodega, a term commonly used in large, overcrowded cities, such as New York City, where space is at a premium, is similar to a small neighborhood convenience store. Waseka says she plans to keep the vibe of a 1920s-era grocery store atmosphere. The family-owned facility aims to have grab-and-go food with tables and chairs near the front windows. It will be located next door to The Kitchenette. “We will probably not have a cat, although we have had many inquiries since a neighborhood cat is a typical bodega element,” Waseka told the St. Cloud Times. The St. Cloud City Council approved the store's tobacco license on Aug. 17. Located at 415 E. St. Germain St., the arrival of St. G's Bodega currently is planned to time with the East Side’s annual Festi-Fall East that occurs Sept. 20. “This store is a puzzle piece that fits right into the rejuvenation concept of creating an urban, walkable entertainment district and definitely benefits the businesses we have next door,” Waseka wrote on Facebook earlier this summer. Earlier this summer, Waseka also bought the former Ace Bar building, which had been closed for a decade. She plans to renovate it and reopen it as a bar and restaurant at some point in the future.

title: Sena and BMW reveal co-developed intercom system ahead of 2026 GS Trophy - Visordown
content: Sena is set to become the official communication provider for riders, marshals and organisers of the 2026 BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy next month. Sena is set to provide 90 communication systems for riders, marshals and organisers of the 2026 BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy, which takes place from September 13-18, in Romania. The intercom specialist will act as an official partner of the race, with teams set to receive BMW ConnectedRide COM P1 GS and Sena 60X units throughout the event. But it’s not just competitors, marshals and the organisers that will benefit from this new partnership, as Sena’s Expand Mesh Multi-Sport headsets will allow photographers and videographers to stay in touch with teams. The new set-up focuses mainly on the BMW ConnectedRide COM P1 GS, with 55 units set to be provided. The system has been co-developed by Sena and BMW, and can be integrated into the new BMW GS Rallye Carbon helmet. To make group communication easier, the system uses Mesh Intercom and combines microphone noise reduction with second-generation HD speakers. As well as the 55 BMW ConnectedRide COM P1 GS, Sena will provide 25 60X systems which feature Mesh Intercom, Sound by Bose and a new joystick designed for use with gloves. Speaking about the new agreement with BMW, Vlada Bokza, European Motorcycle Marketing Manager at SENA, said: “It is at the heart of the action that we truly understand how our intercoms are used, what works perfectly and what we can still improve. There’s a new resident on the Georgia Southern University campus, housed inside the Allen E. Paulson College of Engineering and Computing: A humanoid robot designed to serve as a cornerstone for advanced research and applied, hands-on classroom learning for students. According to a release from Georgia Southern, the robot expands robotics and artificial intelligence initiatives. Unlike traditional industrial robots, the platform is designed to interact in human environments, giving students and faculty opportunities to study human-robot interaction, machine learning and autonomous navigation, the release stated. “This is more than just a piece of equipment; it is a catalyst for innovation at Georgia Southern,” said Rami Haddad, Ph.D., former interim dean of the Paulson College of Engineering and chair of the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. Students across multiple disciplines, including computer science, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and information technology, will collaborate on programming, maintaining and optimizing the platform. “By integrating this humanoid robot into our classrooms and research laboratories, we are giving students hands-on experience with the technologies that are transforming engineering, computing and industry across the world,” Haddad said. The capabilities position Georgia Southern graduates to help meet the growing demand for talent at the region’s logistics centers, automated ports and advanced manufacturing facilities, the release stated. “Investments in advanced technologies like this humanoid robot reinforce Georgia Southern’s commitment to preparing students for the future of work while strengthening the university’s impact on the region,” said Avinandan Mukherjee, Ph.D., provost and executive vice president for Academic Affairs. The robot will be housed in a specialized, multidisciplinary laboratory that will serve as a shared resource for undergraduate projects, master’s theses and faculty-led research. “Our new robot will enhance interdisciplinary research, strengthen experiential learning and equip our graduates with the knowledge and expertise needed to lead in the rapidly evolving fields of robotics, automation and artificial intelligence,” said Abhijit Bhattacharyya, Ph.D., dean of the College of Engineering and Computing. The campus community may also catch a glimpse of the robot going to class, working in the labs and walking around campus.
